status: Single descriptive component comparison; not alignment tracker or forecast

survey.question: As you may know, the 1973 Supreme Court Case Roe v. Wade established a woman's constitutional right to have an abortion. Would you like to see the Supreme Court overturn its Roe v. Wade decision, or not?
survey.response_label_note: Full no-response label on guide page 40 adds maintain abortion rights in all 50 states; raw Stata label is truncated.
survey.weight_rule: Guide page 4 recommends wave-specific genpop weight for cross-sectional analysis.
survey.sample_description: YouGov online panel; 4,943 post-election respondents, drawn from adults invited after the September wave. Do not describe as a simple random sample or restrict to voters without additional filtering.
survey.denominator: All positive-weight November-wave respondents, including not sure and skipped; no yes/no-only renormalization.

court.name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization
court.component: Overruled Roe v. Wade (and Casey); not an estimate of support for every part of the opinion or subsequent restrictions.

interpretation: The weighted survey majority opposed overturning Roe in late 2020; the Court overruled Roe in June 2022. This is disagreement on that named component across those dates, not a contemporaneous estimate or causal claim.
limitations: About 19 months between fieldwork and decision; attitudes may have changed.
Question framing explicitly references a constitutional right and may affect responses.
Panel recruitment, weighting and nonresponse can affect representativeness; no design-based confidence interval or significance claim.
One selected example cannot estimate overall court-public agreement or predictiveness.
Does not assess Mississippi’s fifteen-week limit, all state restrictions, or the constitutional correctness of the decision.
